name: LLM-MCTS (Large Language Models as Commonsense Knowledge for Large-Scale Task Planning)
venue: NeurIPS 2023 (Thirty-seventh Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)
authors_affiliation: Zirui Zhao, Wee Sun Lee, David Hsu — National University of Singapore (NUS), School of Computing.
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single-paper code repo, not a continuously-maintained leaderboard/paper-list)
task_domain: Embodied / decision-making: large-scale, long-horizon household object-rearrangement task planning (robot task planning under partial observation), with additional analysis tasks (multiplication, multi-hop air-travel planning).
problem_setting: Interactive, online, single-agent sequential decision-making in a partially observable, large object-centric domain (VirtualHome). The agent receives a natural-language instruction plus partial observations and must output executable actions to rearrange objects. Modeled as a POMDP solved online by MCTS. Supervision is available only as a small dataset D of expert trajectories/observations used for few-shot prompting and (for one baseline) fine-tuning; no gradient updates to the LLM itself. The LLM (GPT-3.5-turbo, or GPT-2 for a fine-tuned baseline) is used both to induce a commonsense prior belief over states (world model) and a heuristic action policy.
what_is_retrieved: Few-shot demonstrations (expert trajectories): instruction-conditioned (instruction + corresponding expert trajectory) demos retrieved from the expert dataset D to build the K-shot prompt for the LLM heuristic policy. Object/location lists (Dobj) are also drawn from D, and sentence-BERT embeddings are used to map free-form LLM outputs to canonical names.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed offline dataset D of expert trajectories/observations in similar household environments (200 prompt-candidate instances selected from 2000 generated tasks). The retrievable store does not grow during deployment; the per-episode belief is updated but is not a retrievable memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking: the K most similar expert instructions/trajectories (by sentence-BERT cosine similarity to the current instruction) are retrieved as the K-shot prompt. No notion of recovering a complete minimal set or precision-driven variable-size selection.
retrieval_unit: Single demonstration / full expert trajectory: an (instruction, expert-trajectory) demo used as a K-shot exemplar for the policy prompt. (Auxiliary: object-name strings from Dobj for state/goal grounding.)
index_source: Static, offline-induced store: the expert dataset D (generated offline via regression planning with handcrafted heuristics, following Watch-And-Help). A 200-instance subset of D serves as prompt candidates. Frozen after offline construction.
index_structure_topology: Flat embedding index of instructions/demonstrations (sentence-BERT vectors over which cosine similarity is computed). The per-episode state belief is maintained as an object-centric graph (nodes=objects, edges=Inside/On relations), but that is the world-model belief, not the retrieval index.
retriever_type: Dense (off-the-shelf sentence-BERT embeddings + cosine similarity top-K). No BM25, no learned/generative retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf): sentence-BERT (Reimers & Gurevych 2019) is used as a fixed encoder; retrieval is pure cosine-similarity top-K with no training, no contrastive fine-tuning, no LM-feedback or RL signal.
query_construction: Raw natural-language instruction l of the current task is embedded with sentence-BERT and compared (cosine similarity) to embedded instructions l_i in D; the most similar are selected as exemplars. Surface forms of LLM outputs (object positions, actions) are likewise embedded and matched to canonical names in Dobj / admissible action set.
query_granularity: Task-level: the prompt-exemplar retrieval is done once per task using the task's natural-language instruction (one-shot at t=0). The retrieved K-shot prompt is then reused across the LLM policy queries within that task's tree search.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot (per task): exemplars are retrieved once at the start of an episode based on the instruction. Within MCTS the same retrieved K-shot prompt is reused for repeated LLM policy/world-model queries; sentence-BERT matching of LLM responses to canonical names recurs throughout.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (no learned trigger): exemplar retrieval is triggered once per task by the arrival of the instruction; there is no uncertainty/confidence/reflection-based retrieval trigger.
reranking: None: top-K by cosine similarity is used directly with no reranking stage (no cross-encoder, no RRF, no hierarchy-aware rerank).
retrieved_context_refinement: None of the rerank/distill/compress kind for the retrieved demos. The only post-processing is sentence-BERT embedding + cosine-similarity mapping of free-form LLM outputs to canonical object names / admissible actions (a normalization/translation step, not refinement of retrieved exemplars).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation (in-context few-shot): retrieved (instruction, expert-trajectory) pairs are concatenated as a K-shot prompt that conditions the LLM when it acts (a) as the heuristic policy pi(a|h) inside PUCT and (b) as the commonsense world model sampling initial object positions. The LLM outputs are then used as a search heuristic (prior policy) and as a state prior belief, not committed directly as actions.
planning_integration: Inside MCTS / tree search: retrieval-conditioned LLM outputs are embedded inside Monte Carlo Tree Search. The LLM-induced commonsense belief b(s0) provides the prior over states that MCTS samples from at each simulation root; the LLM-induced heuristic policy provides the prior pi(a|h) in the PUCT action-selection rule. Goals and observations are translated to/from natural language. MCTS does look-ahead simulation, expansion, random rollout, and backup; the LLM policy biases exploration but final action choice depends on Q-values and visit counts.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call/per-node within a rollout: the LLM heuristic policy is queried (and sampled M times) at action-selection / node-expansion points during the tree search to form the empirical policy distribution; the world-model belief sampling occurs per simulation at the root. So retrieval-conditioned LLM calls are woven in per simulation/per node rather than once per final answer.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw expert trajectory / natural-language demonstration: the injected exemplars are raw (instruction, action-sequence) trajectories rendered as English sentences (observations and goals translated to natural language), used verbatim as in-context few-shot examples.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw trajectory / single demonstration (verbatim expert (instruction, trajectory) examples). Not distilled strategies, guidelines, or reusable skills.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Primarily MCTS itself: the LLM policy is used only as a soft heuristic prior in PUCT, so action selection is also governed by Q-values and visit counts, tolerating an imperfect/hallucinated policy. A randomness hyper-parameter lambda is mixed into the empirical policy distribution to avoid over-deterministic LLM samples; M-sample averaging approximates the policy distribution; sentence-BERT mapping forces LLM outputs into admissible actions/objects. No retriever-aware training or explicit relevance-evaluator/self-reflection module.
memory_type: none (no persistent cross-task learned memory). A per-episode object-centric belief over states (a graph/probability-vector) is maintained and updated online, but it is reset per task and is not a retrievable experience memory.
write_back: False (no): the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills back into a retrievable store. The expert dataset D is fixed; only the within-episode state belief is updated from observations (transient, not written back to D).
online_growth: No: the retrievable store (expert dataset D / prompt candidates) is frozen after offline construction; it does not grow during deployment/test time.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back to a retrievable memory). The per-episode belief is updated per-step from observations, but that is transient state-estimation, not memory writing.
failure_experience_usage: Not used: failed trajectories are analyzed qualitatively in the paper (policy/model/translation errors) but are not stored or retrieved; the few-shot prompt corpus is expert (success) trajectories only. No success+failure contrastive or failure-only corrective storage.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no persistent memory store is mutated). The transient per-episode belief is delta-updated by Bayesian-style observation updates within an episode but is not a stored/evolving memory.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No: case/exemplar selection is fixed sentence-BERT cosine top-K, not a learned or RL-optimized retrieval policy. (The action policy guidance comes from the LLM heuristic + MCTS, not from a learned retriever.)
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-agent private setting; no sharing of memory/experience across multiple agents or frameworks.
benchmarks: VirtualHome (3D household simulator) object-rearrangement tasks across difficulty splits: Simple, Compositional (Comp.), NovelSimple, NovelComp.(2), NovelComp.(3), each in Seen and Unseen apartment/item settings (2000 tasks generated, 200 used as prompt candidates, 800 for evaluation). Analysis tasks: arithmetic multiplication; multi-hop air-travel planning (Kaggle World Cities + Virtual Radar Server flight routes, 68 large + 62 mid-size cities, 400+400 city-pair tests).
benchmark_family: embodied (VirtualHome) — household object rearrangement / task planning; plus auxiliary symbolic/decision-making analysis tasks (multiplication, multi-hop travel-planning).
baselines: UCT (vanilla MCTS with uniform state prior and ground-truth reward, no commonsense knowledge); Fine-tuned GPT-2 policy (Li et al., trained on 10000 trajectories); GPT-3.5 Policy (LLM-as-policy few-shot, Huang et al. language-planner style). Also referenced: L-Model (LLM as world model only) and L-Policy (LLM as policy only) as conceptual baselines. Ablations: No Heuristic Policy, Uniform State Prior, Fully Observable.
key_metrics: Success rate (%) of completing the task within the step limit (30 steps in main eval), reported as mean ± standard error across difficulty splits and Seen/Unseen settings. Travel-planning uses path/flight-route accuracy.
headline_result: On VirtualHome, GPT3.5-MCTS outperforms both MCTS-alone (UCT: 0% across all splits) and LLM-as-policy baselines by a wide margin, with the largest gains on novel/complex tasks: on the hardest split NovelComp.(3)-Seen it reaches 33.6±3.1% vs GPT3.5 Policy 5.4±2.0% and fine-tuned GPT-2 2.3±1.5%; on NovelComp.(2)-Seen 72.6±6.9% vs 48.2% (GPT3.5 Policy); on Simple-Seen 91.4±3.3% vs 83.4% (GPT3.5 Policy).
ablations: Three ablations on the GPT3.5-MCTS framework: (1) No Heuristic Policy (UCT with LLM-induced commonsense belief but NO LLM PUCT guidance) collapses to 0.0±0.0% on all splits — the LLM heuristic policy is essential to make the search tractable. (2) Uniform State Prior (replace LLM commonsense belief with uniform prior) drops to ~0-3% — the LLM world-model prior is essential. (3) Fully Observable (give MCTS perfect state knowledge) raises success only modestly above the partial-observation LLM-MCTS (e.g. Simple-Seen 94.0 vs 91.4; NovelComp.(3)-Unseen 76.6 vs 70.4), indicating the LLM-induced belief is already fairly accurate and partial observability is not the main bottleneck. Together these show both components (commonsense world model + heuristic policy) are necessary, with search-space reduction via the policy heuristic being the dominant driver.
evaluation_decoupling: Not decoupled in the RAG sense: no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are reported. Evaluation is end-to-end task success rate; the travel-planning analysis adds a separate path/flight-accuracy intrinsic measure for the world-model-vs-policy comparison, and a failure-mode breakdown (policy/model/translation errors) is given.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (task success rate within a step budget). Some process-level analysis is provided qualitatively: failure analysis attributing errors to policy/model/translation, and the MDL/travel-planning analysis examining intermediate world-model accuracy vs policy generalization.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Compute is driven by MCTS rollouts and repeated LLM sampling: default run uses simulation_num=100 simulations, simulation_per_act=2, M samples per LLM policy/world-model query, max_depth=20, max_episode_len=50 (per the released config). The central efficiency argument is that the LLM heuristic policy drastically reduces the effective search space (vanilla UCT is intractable, scoring 0%), trading extra LLM API calls for vastly fewer effective rollouts; explicit wall-clock/latency/token-cost numbers are not the headline (no quantified token/$ budget reported).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-K few-shot: top-K most similar expert instructions/trajectories are retrieved as the K-shot prompt (K is a fixed hyper-parameter; world-model belief uses 3 fixed prompt examples for response format). Prompt candidates are restricted to a 200-instance subset of D to demonstrate small-training-set performance. No adaptive/budget-capped/precision-driven k selection. [uncertain] exact K value for the policy K-shot prompt.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method/empirical paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark-contribution paper). Note for context: 2000 VirtualHome tasks generated (following Watch-And-Help), 200 selected as prompt candidates, 800 used for evaluation; expert trajectories collected via regression planning with handcrafted heuristics under full observation; travel-planning ground truth from Virtual Radar Server flight routes over Kaggle World Cities.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not framed as case-based reasoning). If forced to map: only a weak Retrieve phase (similarity-based exemplar retrieval) is present; no Reuse-as-adaptation, Revise, or Retain. Flags: [Retrieve=partial, Reuse=no, Revise=no, Retain=no].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False: the paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. Retrieval is incidental few-shot prompt selection, not CBR.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/APIs are retrieved; not a tool-use method).
index_content_separation: N/A (no lightweight-index-then-content / progressive-disclosure separation; flat demo index only).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index or integration protocol; not a tool-use method).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling; not a tool-use method).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A / verbatim ICL exemplar: retrieved expert trajectories are used as verbatim in-context examples with no case adaptation/revision (not a CBR adaptation pipeline).
builds_on: Monte Carlo Tree Search / PUCT (Kocsis & Szepesvari UCT; Silver et al. AlphaGo-style PUCT with policy prior); LLM-as-policy task planners (Huang et al. language-planner / 'Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners', SayCan-style line); fine-tuned GPT-2 interactive-decision policy (Li et al., Pre-Trained LMs for Interactive Decision-Making); VirtualHome and Watch-And-Help (Puig et al.) for environment/data; sentence-BERT (Reimers & Gurevych) for embedding-based name/exemplar matching; LLM-to-formal-goal translation (Xie et al.). MCTS implementation adapted from MC-LAVE-RL.
contrasts_with: L-Policy (using the LLM directly as the committed policy, e.g. GPT-3.5 Policy / fine-tuned GPT-2 policy) and L-Model (using the LLM only as a world model with planning, which performs poorly alone due to search-space size); vanilla UCT/MCTS without commonsense knowledge (intractable, 0%). Also contrasts with prior work using LLMs only as MCTS heuristics or transition functions on small-scale reasoning/coding (e.g., LLM-as-heuristic, LLM-as-transition), arguing those did not exploit LLMs as a full commonsense world model for large-scale planning.
lineage: Group C (RAG/LLM planning): sits in the lineage of LLM-guided search/planning that injects LLM knowledge into a classical search algorithm (MCTS). It bridges LLM-as-policy planners (SayCan/Zero-Shot-Planner) and model-based search; a precursor to later LLM+MCTS/tree-search reasoning-and-planning methods (e.g., RAP/Reasoning-via-Planning, LATS, ToT-style search). Retrieval here is light (similarity-based few-shot exemplar selection) rather than a central RAG memory component.
